messages:
matt: Quick question for the audit team — the external compliance folks asked for a full 'who did what' export for the last 6 months. Can we include user email addresses in the export or is it only internal IDs? Also what format do we currently export in (CSV/NDJSON/jsonl)?

janelle: We store actor info as `principal_id` + `principal_type`. Email isn't in every log row unless the action was performed via an identity-linked flow (SSO provisioning, invite accept).

amy: We avoid exporting PII by default. For hosted customers we redact email unless there's an explicit admin consent/contract. See policy: https://internal.redwood.com/policies/audit-exports :lock:

raj: For format: internal export tool outputs newline-delimited JSON (jsonl) with these top-level fields: `ts, org_id, principal_id, principal_type, action, resource, metadata`

security-bot: Retention policy reminder: hosted default = 365 days, Dedicated customers can request longer retention via contract. On-prem/private: retention controlled by customer. Export approvals required for PII-containing exports. (https://internal.redwood.com/policies/retention)

matt: OK, good to know. The auditors explicitly want email+IP for identity mapping. Is there an approval path to include emails?

janelle: We can do a scoped export if Security approves and product signs off. Process: open #security-requests ticket with reason + requester, then Security will review and approve. After approval infra runs `redwood-audit export` to a scoped S3 bucket with SSE.

amy: Example command we use internally (ops only):
```
redwood-audit export \--org acme-corp \--from 2025-09-01 \--to 2026-03-01 \--fields ts,principal_id,principal_email,action,resource,ip \--out s3://redwood-exports/acme/audit-1769223456.jsonl \```
Note: `principal_email` column is only populated when permitted.

raj: Also check that the exported file has `encryption: AES256` and we attach a restricted ACL. We push temporary presigned links (24h) to the requester and log the export action back into the audit trail.

matt: Who can actually kick off that `redwood-audit export`? I don't want to accidentally run something that includes PII.

janelle: Only people in the `audit-exports` group (Security, SRE on-call, and a Product lead) have the role to run exports that include `principal_email`. Regular infra engineers can run exports with non-PII fields.

amy: If you need to map identities for the auditor, we can do a one-off mapping table export (email <-> principal_id) under SEC approval; that keeps the main logs PII-free.

matt: Perfect — I'll open the #security-requests ticket now and tag you both. Thanks :thumbsup:

janelle: Ping me in the ticket, I'll queue the export after approval and share the presigned link.

security-bot: Action logged: export-request-created by matt at 1769223456; request_id=exp-20260316-42. Approval required from security@redwood.com.

matt: Filed ticket: https://tickets.internal.redwood.com/exp-20260316-42 — adding the auditors' scope and requested fields.

raj: FYI — when exporting, prefer `--compress gz` to reduce transfer size and double-check the checksum after upload.

amy: Also add a README in the S3 folder describing what fields are included and the approval docs. Keeps auditors happy.

matt: Will do. Thanks all!
